comparisons.peer_summary: The provision for credit losses increased $1.5 billion to $883 million, primarily driven by the commercial real estate office portfolio compared to a benefit in the prior year.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC report specific provision for credit losses driven by commercial real estate exposures in 2024, but with diverging trends and magnitudes. MS reported a provision of $202 million, where the commercial real estate component was partially offset by macroeconomic improvements. In contrast, BAC reported a significantly higher provision of $883 million, which increased $1.5 billion from the prior year and was primarily driven by its commercial real estate office portfolio, contrasting with a benefit in the prior year.

comparisons.comparison: MS and JPM both identified commercial real estate as a key driver of credit losses, though their provision outcomes differed. MS reported a $202 million provision driven by specific commercial real estate loans. JPM reported a lower total provision of $762 million, with net charge-offs of $617 million primarily concentrated in Real Estate/Office. JPM also highlighted a $145 million net addition to its allowance driven by real estate downgrades and the inclusion of the First Republic portfolio, whereas MS noted improvements in the macroeconomic outlook partially offsetting its specific CRE provisions.
